title: Worksheet 12: Robots and Sensors
directions: Read the paragraph below carefully. Then answer all questions using ONLY the information in the paragraph. Circle the letter of the best answer.
paragraph: A robot is a machine that can sense its environment, process information, and take physical action to complete a task, often automatically or with limited human control. Sensors are a critical part of nearly every robot, because they allow the robot to gather information about the world around it, similar to how human senses like sight and touch provide information to the brain. Common robot sensors include ultrasonic or infrared sensors, which measure distance to nearby objects to help a robot avoid obstacles, light sensors, which detect brightness or specific colors, and touch or pressure sensors, which detect physical contact. Once a sensor collects information, it sends that data to the robot's controller, which acts like the robot's brain, deciding what action to take based on the sensor data and the instructions programmed by its designer. Without sensors, a robot would be unable to react to changes in its environment and could only follow a fixed set of movements regardless of what was actually happening around it.
